content: Document text extraction for ingestion pipelines (2026): PyMuPDF is fastest (~0.01s/page) but AGPL-licensed, which matters for a distributed product; pymupdf4llm adds to_markdown() with headings/tables and is the speed+quality sweet spot for clean digital PDFs but inherits AGPL. pypdf is pure-Python, permissive (BSD), no system deps, ~0.024s/page, with occasional spacing artifacts - the right default for a local-first tool that must pip-install cleanly. pdfplumber (built on pdfminer.six, MIT) is the choice when tables/coordinates matter. Docling and unstructured give the best semantic segmentation but are heavy installs (ML models) and slow. DOCX: python-docx. Markdown/txt need no library. Recommended pipeline discipline: attach provenance metadata (source, page, parser name, timestamp) to every extracted unit; keep the extractor behind a per-format dispatch so it can be swapped.
